system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller Draft (SPA Update and Disclosure Letter)

**Scope note:** I reviewed the Seller counsel's cover note, the SPA "Key Negotiated Positions" summary, and the Disclosure Letter against the Buyer playbook. I have not seen the full SPA draft, so clause references below are as the Seller summarises them. Check each point against the full mark-up before responding.

## Headline view

The package departs from the playbook on almost every material point. Several positions are not fallbacks but outright moves against us: fundamental warranties pulled into the general regime, a blanket limitation and reliance regime with no fraud carve-out, and consent-on-delivery for a customer that is about 30% of revenue. The Seller's framing (market standard, "FINAL", "settled at principal level") does not change the analysis. We have no record of any principal-level agreement to these terms, and no written authority from Amelia Frost exists for any fallback.

## Departures from playbook

| Issue | Seller position | Playbook position | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| General cap (12.1) | 20% / AUD 4.8m | 25% / AUD 6.0m. 20% is a fallback needing Frost's written authority identifying the draft | Departs; no authority given |
| De minimis (12.2) | AUD 25,000 | AUD 5,000 | Departs |
| Basket (12.2) | AUD 250,000, deductible (excess only) | AUD 50,000, tipping (first dollar once exceeded) | Departs materially |
| General time limit (12.3/13) | 18 months | 24 months (18 months needs Frost approval) | Departs; no approval |
| Time-limit spillover | Any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly excluded | Keep categories separate; no hidden general-regime override | Departs |
| Title/capacity (Fundamental) | Same caps and time limits as general warranties | 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar | **Critical departure** |
| Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance (9.3/12.8/20.5) | Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of everything | **Critical departure** |
| Disclosure (Sch 7; DL 1.1, 1.2) | Whole data room, Accounts, statutory registers, public records | Specific fair disclosure only; reject deemed disclosure | Departs |
| Buyer knowledge (8.3) | Excludes anything Buyer or advisers knew, including anything discoverable in the data room or public records | Delete blanket exclusions; any qualifier needs named Seller knowledge persons and reasonable enquiry; never for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities | Departs |
| Bluefen (3/6.3) | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery | Effective consent and evidence conditions satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours insufficient | Departs |
| Riverlark (2/7) | Release to be provided after Completion | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective releases; post-completion release only with irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval | Departs |
| Employee bonuses (DL 5) | Seller matter; not in funds flow | AUD 420k plus on-costs as a specific line item or seller-funded | Departs |
| Ironquay IP (11.1) | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; "adequate" | Broaden indemnity; preserve SOW3 cure; AUD 180k unverified | Departs |
| DD-006 export incident (4.6; Sch 6) | "Not expected to be material" | Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; no assumption either way | Departs (conclusion asserted) |
| Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | Ordinary-course operating costs | Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction | Departs (conclusion asserted) |
| Tax/IP | Settled under general regime | Remain open; no unlimited liability assumed; no resolution assumed | Departs; reject |
| Title (DL 10) | Share register (DD-012) is evidence | DD-012 is an internal supplied source, not independent proof | Departs |

## Reasoning on the material issues

**1. Fundamental and title warranties in the general regime.** This is the most serious point. Title and capacity are the foundation of what we are buying. Putting them under a 20% cap, an 18-month limit and a deductible basket means that if title to the shares is defective, we could be left with AUD 4.8m of recovery at most, after 18 months, with the first AUD 250k unrecoverable. The Seller's "administrative simplicity" rationale is not a reason to accept this. Reject outright.

**2. Fraud carve-out.** The Seller's blanket application of limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature" has no fraud exception. The playbook says fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct must be carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable, and no one can waive this. Insist on this language expressly, and check that the non-reliance clause does not bar fraud claims.

**3. Disclosure and buyer knowledge together.** Combined, these shift risk onto us. The Seller's general disclosure (DL 1.1, 1.2) would deem the whole data room disclosed. Clause 8.3 would then exclude anything we could have found there. Together they would make most of the diligence record a defence to our claims. Both must go. Disclosure must be specific and fair, and buyer knowledge should be deleted or limited to named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry, and never applied to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

**4. Bluefen consent.** The disclosure itself says no final Bluefen consent is in the data room and conditions are not evidenced. Yet the Seller proposes to treat consent as satisfied on delivery and offers only reasonable endeavours. Bluefen is roughly AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue (about 30%). Require effective consent and evidence that all conditions in clause 11.3 are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours is not sufficient for a material customer consent.

**5. Riverlark.** The facility is about AUD 3.2m and is not repaid. A release "following Completion" leaves the security in place and the Company exposed, with no payout mechanism. Require payout at Completion from the funds flow, a direct repayment to Riverlark, and effective security releases. A post-completion release is acceptable only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.

**6. Employee bonuses.** The bonuses (AUD 420k) are excluded from the funds flow, and the disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply. Calling it "a matter for the Seller" does not protect us if the liability sits in the Company post-Completion. Require either a specific line item in the funds flow or seller funding, including triggered on-costs. Ask the Seller to calculate the on-costs.

**7. Ironquay IP.** The indemnity is limited to the SOW3 payment, which is not adequate. Broaden it to cover the IP and related claims arising from the Ironquay matter. Preserve the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180k open amount is not verified either way. Obtain bank evidence of non-payment or payment, and any confirmatory assignment. Do not assume the figure is correct or incorrect.

**8. DD-006 export incident.** The Seller says it is "not expected to be material", but the disclosure states the investigation is preliminary, scope is unknown, and it is not known whether anyone accessed the file or whether notification is required. Under the playbook we assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. Require log preservation, investigation, and regular updates. Obtain privacy counsel's view on notification. Consider whether a specific indemnity is appropriate. The Seller's materiality conclusion should not be accepted.

**9. Sandbar renewals.** The Seller calls them ordinary-course, and the disclosure does not say whether they are terminable or accrued. Assess them properly. Do not reclassify them as Debt or deduct from price automatically. Check their timing relative to Completion.

**10. Tax and IP.** The Seller says these are settled under the general regime. They are not. Tax and IP positions remain open. We should not assume unlimited liability, but we also should not accept a general-regime cap.

**11. Title evidence.** The Seller relies on the share register (DD-012) as proof of title. The playbook treats this as an internal supplied source, not independent evidence. Require independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority. Examples include an ASIC company extract, the share transfer history, a PPSR search, and board and authority records.

**12. Lease and Mossvale.** These are not in the playbook but need assessment. The disclosure says the lease requires notification, not consent, and that Mossvale's restriction does not expressly require consent. The Seller's "no admission" language (DL 1.4) does not answer whether consent is in fact required. Get a NSW legal view on whether either counterparty's consent is needed and, if so, treat it as a condition.

**13. "Settled" and "FINAL" language.** The Seller says the positions were settled at principal level. Confirm with Amelia Frost whether any such agreement exists before responding. Unless she confirms it, do not treat these positions as agreed.

**14. Data room date.** The disclosure is as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026. Today is 5 November 2026. Request a bring-down disclosure and updated data room index before signing.

## Recommendations (summary)

1. **Reject** the Seller's 12.1 cap (20%) and time limit (18 months) as no fallback authority has been given. Restore 25%/AUD 6m and 24 months.
2. **Reject** the AUD 25k de minimis and AUD 250k deductible basket. Restore AUD 5k de minimis and AUD 50k tipping basket.
3. **Reject** putting title and capacity under the general regime. Restore the separate Fundamental regime: 100% cap, at least 6 years, outside the basket, de minimis and knowledge bar.
4. **Carve out** fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance.
5. **Reject** general disclosure of the data room, Accounts and public registers. Require specific fair disclosure.
6. **Delete** clause 8.3 blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion. Limit any qualifier to named Seller knowledge persons with reasonable enquiry, and never for title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
7. **Require** effective Bluefen consent and evidence of conditions before Completion. Reject consent-on-delivery and reasonable-endeavours-only.
8. **Require** Riverlark payout from Completion funds and effective security releases. Any post-completion release needs an irrevocable undertaking and Frost approval.
9. **Require** the AUD 420k bonuses plus on-costs as a specific funds flow line or seller-funded.
10. **Broaden** the Ironquay indemnity, preserve the SOW3 cure, and obtain bank evidence on the AUD 180k.
11. **Require** DD-006 log preservation, investigation and updates. Obtain privacy counsel's view. Do not accept the "not material" conclusion.
12. **Assess** the Sandbar renewals without automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
13. **Keep** tax and IP open and separate from the general regime.
14. **Require** independent title evidence beyond DD-012.
15. **Assess** lease and Mossvale consent requirements under NSW law.
16. **Confirm** with Amelia Frost whether any principal-level agreement exists before treating the Seller's positions as settled.
17. **Request** a bring-down disclosure and updated data room index.

Before issuing a mark-up, I recommend NSW counsel review the final SPA language, particularly the carve-outs, the Fundamental regime and the Bluefen and Riverlark conditions.
=== END ADVICE ===
